title: Size-Optimized Depth-Constrained Large Parallel Prefix Circuits
problem: Current adder design methods target regular bitwidths and cannot efficiently generate large adders (1024-2048 bits) needed for cryptography. When integrated into circuits like MACs with non-uniform input arrival times, these methods fail to produce optimized designs.
motivation: Large adders are critical for cryptographic applications and when integrated into complex circuits like multiplier-accumulators with non-uniform input timing, efficient design methods become essential.
method: The algorithm designs adders (circuits that add numbers) where the input bits arrive at different times—a common hardware challenge. It breaks the design problem into a divide-and-conquer approach: at each level, combining pairs of bit-groups into larger groups. As it builds, it uses dynamic programming—storing the best partial designs and discarding others that won't lead to better final circuits.
key_novelty: The key insight is treating adder design as a divide-and-conquer problem that naturally lets dynamic programming select the best partial designs at each step.
contributions: Novel algorithm for generating high-quality large adders with non-uniform input arrival time handling
Divide-and-conquer-friendly problem formulation enabling efficient adder synthesis
Dynamic programming approach for maintaining useful adder structures during generation
Achieved 2.8% delay, 8.3% area, and 10.3% power improvements over commercial synthesis tools
limitations: Limitations and generalizability to other circuit types not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Optimized adder design for non-uniform timing constraints
